pharm: Nucleoside metabolic inhibitor; S-phase-specific antimetabolite blocking DNA polymerase
summary: Cytarabine (cytosine arabinoside, ara-C) is an S-phase-specific antimetabolite used, in combination with other agents, for remission induction in acute non-lymphocytic (myeloid) leukemia in adults and children, and also for acute lymphocytic leukemia and the blast phase of CML. Given IV, subcutaneously, or intrathecally (preservative-free only) for meningeal leukemia. Its principal toxicity is profound bone marrow suppression, so it must be used by clinicians experienced in cancer chemotherapy with full supportive care.
indications: Remission induction of acute non-lymphocytic (myeloid) leukemia, in combination, in adults and children
Blast phase of chronic myelogenous leukemia
Prophylaxis and treatment of meningeal leukemia (intrathecal, preservative-free)

dosage.d: 100 mg/m2/day by continuous infusion (days 1-7) OR 100 mg/m2 IV every 12 hours (days 1-7)

dosage.n: High neurotoxicity/ocular toxicity risk; give prophylactic steroid eye drops

admin: Administer only under supervision of a clinician experienced in cytotoxic chemotherapy
Use single-dose preservative-free solutions for intrathecal use
Continuous IV infusion is generally better tolerated than rapid injection
Provide antiemetics; give prophylactic corticosteroid eye drops with high-dose therapy
Handle as a hazardous cytotoxic drug; ensure marrow and supportive resources are available
moa: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog; intracellularly phosphorylated to ara-CTP, which inhibits DNA polymerase and is incorporated into DNA, blocking DNA synthesis (S-phase-specific cytotoxicity).

relative: Pre-existing severe bone marrow suppression (use only with weighed benefit/risk)
Hepatic or renal impairment (higher toxicity, especially high-dose)

preg: Can cause fetal harm; congenital malformations reported. Avoid in pregnancy; advise effective contraception.
lact: Unknown whether excreted in milk; because of potential serious adverse effects, discontinue nursing.
renal: Renal impairment increases risk of CNS toxicity with high-dose regimens; reduce dose and monitor closely.
hepatic: Hepatic dysfunction may increase CNS toxicity; use cautiously, consider dose reduction, and monitor liver function.

major: Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy / radiation — additive marrow toxicity
Live vaccines — risk of disseminated infection; avoid
moderate: Digoxin (oral tablets) — cytarabine may reduce digoxin absorption; monitor levels
Gentamicin — antagonism against K. pneumoniae reported
Flucytosine — cytarabine may reduce its antifungal efficacy
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate uric acid (tumor lysis); monitor.

serious: Severe bone marrow suppression (leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia)
Cytarabine (ara-C) syndrome — fever, myalgia, bone pain, rash, conjunctivitis, malaise

monitoring: Frequent complete blood counts and bone marrow during induction
counsel: Report fever, sore throat, or any sign of infection immediately
Flu-like symptoms (ara-C syndrome) may occur 6-12 hours after a dose
Use effective contraception during and after therapy
pk: Cytotoxic during S-phase after intracellular activation
Immediate with IV; SC peak about 20-60 min
20-25 C (68-77 F); reconstituted solution per label
pearls: Boxed warning: principal toxicity is bone marrow suppression; use only with adequate supportive care
High-dose ara-C causes cerebellar toxicity and conjunctivitis — give prophylactic steroid eye drops and assess neurology before each dose
Intrathecal use must be preservative-free single-dose solution
Watch for tumor lysis syndrome at start of leukemia treatment
missed: Administered on a scheduled chemotherapy protocol by clinicians; missed or delayed doses are managed by the oncology team, not self-administered.
overdose: No antidote. Overdose causes severe, potentially irreversible CNS toxicity and profound myelosuppression. Discontinue, provide intensive supportive care, transfusions, and treat infection.
